docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A scene with a Player and floors with a Static collider, so Play lets you walk.
  • Fixed-point math: there are no decimal literals.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Event-driven. Everything responds to events; nothing polls in onUpdate.
  • The scene script as controller. Shared functions live in the scene script and are published to _G, so object scripts can call them. See Lua scripting.
  • One-time flags. A local boolean stops an action from repeating.

docs.title: Tutorial: Animated Doors
docs.text:
A door that opens and closes on a button press, using an animation built in the timeline.

You will use the Timeline, an Interactable, Animation.Play with onComplete, and Animation.IsPlaying.

docs.title: 1. The door
docs.text: Add a Mesh object for the door and name it exactly Door. The name is how the animation finds it.

docs.title: 2. The animations
docs.text:
1. Open View > Timeline, choose New animation, and name it door_open.
  2. Set Length to 30 (one second).
  3. Add track: Object > Position, target Door.
  4. Scrub to frame 0 and double-click the lane to key the door's closed position. Scrub to frame 30, move the door where it should end up (for example 3 m up), and key it there.
  5. Make a second animation, door_close, with the same two keys reversed.

docs.title: 3. Interaction
docs.text: On the Door, Add component > Interactable. The defaults work: Cross button, radius 2 m, repeatable. Turn on Show prompt and pick a canvas if you have one with a "Press X" message.

docs.title: 4. Sounds
docs.text: Add two Audio clip objects named door_open and door_close, each with a WAV.

docs.title: 5. The script
docs.text:
On the Door, New Lua in the Script component:

local isOpen = false

function onInteract(self)
    -- Ignore presses while an animation runs
    if Animation.IsPlaying("door_open") or Animation.IsPlaying("door_close") then
        return
    end

    Interact.SetEnabled(self, false)

    if isOpen then
        isOpen = false
        Audio.Play("door_close", 100, 64)
        Animation.Play("door_close", {
            onComplete = function() Interact.SetEnabled(self, true) end
        })
    else
        isOpen = true
        Audio.Play("door_open", 100, 64)
        Animation.Play("door_open", {
            onComplete = function() Interact.SetEnabled(self, true) end
        })
    end
end

docs.title: 6. Play
docs.text: Walk up and press Cross to open; press again to close. You cannot interrupt the animation, the prompt hides while it plays, and onComplete turns interaction back on.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Animation.IsPlaying stops overlapping animations.
  2. Interact.SetEnabled(self, false) hides the prompt and blocks presses.
  3. Animation.Play starts the animation and calls onComplete when it ends.
  4. isOpen remembers which way to go next.

No collision

This door has no collider, so the player can walk through it open or shut. A Static collider feeds the navigation bake at export, and a door that slides away later does not change that bake. To keep the player out, put a Trigger box or an invisible wall where the door is, and treat the door as scenery you animate.

docs.title: Tutorial: Collectible Pickups
docs.text:
Objects the player walks into to collect, with a score on the HUD and a sound.

You will use onCollideWithPlayer, Entity.SetActive, Audio.Play, Persist and UI text.

docs.title: 1. The HUD
docs.text:
1. Open the UI tab. In the canvas picker choose New canvas and name it hud in the inspector.
  2. Click + in the element list and add a Text. Name it score and set its text to Score: 0. Drag it to the top left.

docs.title: 2. The scene script
docs.text:
Select nothing, and under Script in the scene settings click New Lua. Paste:

local scoreText = -1

function onSceneCreationEnd()
    local hud = UI.FindCanvas("hud")
    if hud >= 0 then
        scoreText = UI.FindElement(hud, "score")
        updateScoreDisplay()
    end
end

function updateScoreDisplay()
    if scoreText >= 0 then
        UI.SetText(scoreText, "Score: " .. (Persist.Get("score") or 0))
    end
end

function addScore(amount)
    Persist.Set("score", (Persist.Get("score") or 0) + amount)
    updateScoreDisplay()
end

-- Publish so object scripts can call these
_G.addScore = addScore

docs.title: 3. The pickup
docs.text:
1. Add a Mesh object (a small crate or gem) and give it a Collider with shape Dynamic. Only dynamic colliders are tested against the player, so only they fire onCollideWithPlayer.
  2. On the object click New Lua in its Script component, and paste:
local collected = false

function onCollideWithPlayer(self)
    if collected then return end
    collected = true

    Audio.Play("collect", 127, 64)
    Entity.SetActive(self, false)
    addScore(100)
end
  1. Duplicate the object (Ctrl+D) a few times and place the copies around the scene. Each copy has its own collected flag.

docs.title: 4. The sound
docs.text: Add an Audio clip object, pick a short WAV, and set Name to collect. See Audio.

docs.title: 5. Play
docs.text: Press Play (F5), click the game, and walk into a pickup. It disappears, plays the sound, and the score goes up by 100.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. onCollideWithPlayer fires every frame the player overlaps the object. The collected flag makes it run once.
  2. Entity.SetActive(self, false) hides the object.
  3. addScore runs in the scene script, because it was published to _G. It stores the score in Persist, which survives scene loads, and updates the text.

docs.title: With blocks
docs.text: The pickup is a when the player touches me stack: if not collected then set collected to true, play sound collect, hide self, change score by 100. Make collected and score variables of that script. The score would then live in that script instead of Persist, so use Lua for the scene script if other scenes need the score.

docs.title: Tutorial: Health & Damage
docs.text:
Hazard and healing zones and a health bar that changes colour.

You will use a UI Progress bar, UI.SetProgress, UI.SetProgressColors, PSXMath.Clamp and Trigger boxes.

docs.title: 1. The health bar
docs.text: In the UI tab, make a canvas named hud if you do not have one, + a Progress bar, and name it health. Set its Value to 100 and place it near a corner.

docs.title: 2. Health in the scene script
docs.text:
Select nothing and New Lua under Script. Paste:

local health = 100
local healthBar = -1

function updateHealthBar()
    if healthBar < 0 then return end
    UI.SetProgress(healthBar, health)

    if health > 50 then
        UI.SetProgressColors(healthBar, 0, 40, 0, 0, 255, 0)      -- green
    elseif health > 25 then
        UI.SetProgressColors(healthBar, 40, 40, 0, 255, 255, 0)   -- yellow
    else
        UI.SetProgressColors(healthBar, 40, 0, 0, 255, 0, 0)      -- red
    end
end

function onSceneCreationEnd()
    local hud = UI.FindCanvas("hud")
    if hud >= 0 then
        healthBar = UI.FindElement(hud, "health")
        updateHealthBar()
    end
end

function applyDamage(amount)
    health = PSXMath.Clamp(health - amount, 0, 100)
    updateHealthBar()
    if health <= 0 then
        Controls.SetEnabledPlayer1(false)
        Scene.Load(Scene.GetIndex())    -- reload this scene
    end
end

function applyHeal(amount)
    health = PSXMath.Clamp(health + amount, 0, 100)
    updateHealthBar()
end

_G.applyDamage = applyDamage
_G.applyHeal = applyHeal

docs.title: 3. A damage zone
docs.text:
Add Object > Trigger box, size it over the hazard, and New Lua on its Script field:

function onTriggerEnter()
    applyDamage(25)
end

docs.title: 4. A healing zone
docs.text:
Another Trigger box in a safe spot:

function onTriggerEnter()
    applyHeal(50)
end

docs.title: 5. Play
docs.text: Walk into the damage zone: the bar drops and goes yellow, then red. Walk into the healing zone to refill it. At zero the scene reloads.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. onTriggerEnter fires when the player walks into the box.
  2. PSXMath.Clamp keeps health between 0 and 100.
  3. updateHealthBar sets the fill and the colours from thresholds.
  4. At zero, Scene.Load(Scene.GetIndex()) reloads the current scene, a simple restart. The scene script runs again, so health is back to 100.

docs.title: Ideas
docs.text:
• A cooldown flag stops a zone from hurting every time the player steps in.
  • Use onCollideWithPlayer on a Dynamic collider for a pickup that heals.
  • Show a message on a Text element when health runs out.

docs.title: Tutorial: Scene Transitions
docs.text:
A trigger that moves the player from one scene to another.

You will use the build list, a Trigger box, Scene.Load and Persist.

docs.title: 1. Two scenes
docs.text:
1. Open the scene you have and File > Save As... a second one in the same project folder, for example dungeon.scene. Both keep the Player and floors.
  2. Select nothing and open Build scenes in the scene settings. Add scene for each scene, with the hub first.

Scene numbers are positions in this list: Scene.Load(0) opens the first, Scene.Load(1) the second. Play and Export start at scene 0.

docs.title: 2. A portal in the hub
docs.text:
1. Add Object > Trigger box. Move it over the doorway and set its Size.
  2. In its Script field click New Lua and paste:
function onTriggerEnter()
    Persist.Set("came_from", Scene.GetIndex())
    Scene.Load(1)
end

docs.title: 3. A portal back
docs.text:
Do the same in the second scene, loading scene 0:

function onTriggerEnter()
    Persist.Set("came_from", Scene.GetIndex())
    Scene.Load(0)
end

docs.title: 4. Read it on arrival
docs.text:
In either scene's script (scene settings, Script > File):

function onSceneCreationStart()
    local from = Persist.Get("came_from") or -1
    if from >= 0 then
        Debug.Log("Arrived from scene " .. from)
    end
end

docs.title: 5. Play
docs.text: Press Play. Both scenes in the list are exported. Walk into the trigger in the first scene and you arrive in the second, and back.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The player enters the box and onTriggerEnter fires.
  2. Persist.Set keeps the number across the load; it holds 16 numbers and is lost on power-off.
  3. Scene.Load(i) asks for the transition. It happens at the end of the frame, so code after the call still runs.
  4. The engine loads the new scene's files and runs its scripts.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• For a long load, set a loading screen in the scene settings. Its progress bar must be named loading.
  • In blocks, load scene takes the scene number, and when the player enters the trigger is the event.
